hints.title: String Shift Inefficiency Obstacle
hints.text: Removing adjacent duplicates repeatedly with string replacements causes repeated shifts and quadratic runtime. How can checking each character against the most recently kept character collapse chained duplicates in one pass?

hints.title: Adjacent Pair Cancellation Invariant
hints.text: When two identical adjacent characters are cancelled, characters to their left and right become adjacent. Maintaining a sequential character buffer handles newly formed adjacent pairs immediately.

hints.title: Running Buffer Cancellation Procedure
hints.text: Initialize an empty list. For each character ch in s: if the list is non-empty and its last character equals ch, pop the last character; otherwise append ch. Return the joined list as a string.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of string s (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Single pass where each character is added and removed at most once.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Repeatedly searching for and slicing adjacent duplicate pairs in a string runs in O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Using an auxiliary character buffer collapses adjacent pairs in strictly linear O(N) time and memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing the equivalence of duplicate cancellation to parenthesis matching.
